correctness.rationale: For the prefix ending at zero-based index j, overlap-freeness reduces curling number to detection of a square suffix. Brown et al.'s Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.2 supply the four base squares and exact morphism alignment. The unscaled squares start odd and end even; the scaled ones start even and desubstitute at every odd endpoint, giving U(2m+1)=U(m). At 2m the length-two condition is t_(m-1) != t_m. The length-six window is (1-a,b,1-b,c,1-c,d), where (a,b,c,d) are the four desubstituted letters ending at m; period three is equivalent to a=b != c=d. This is disjoint from the length-two condition and is absent for m<3. Thus 1+Q(M)-J(M) counts square-free suffix endpoints of even index among the first M such endpoints, where Q counts equal adjacent letters and J counts 0011 or 1100 in the length-M word. For complete dyadic blocks Q_s=2^(s-1)-1-Q_(s-1). The factors counted by J_s correspond to alternating triples in the half word, of which there are two per equal adjacent pair in the quarter word, with both shifts fitting. Hence J_s=2Q_(s-2). Together with A(4)=3 this gives increments (2^(r-1)+10)/6 for even r and (2^(r-1)+8)/6 for odd r, proving the formula for all r>=2. Arbitrary-prefix Q obeys the even/odd halving recurrences, giving Q(M)=M/3+O(1+log M). Rounding J to a multiple of four changes it by at most three occurrences; hence J(M)=M/6+O(1+log M). After subtracting N/6, halving the endpoint sum costs O(1+log N) per step, proving the discrepancy and the limit. The uploaded script and output were inspected, not executed. An independent exhaustive square-suffix search at endpoints 0 through 255 reproduced the dyadic counts 3,5,8,12,19,31,54 for exponents 2 through 8. evidence: Brown et al. prove the position alignment for every scaled square and give a starting-position automaton in Theorem 4.3/Figure 6 and relations for root length C. Their Section 3 defines the cumulative A(i), B(i) by start position, and Theorem 4.6 counts distinct squares under that convention. Caveney et al. distinguish the indexing conventions and study repetition avoidance for constructed words in the passages examined.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A bound on starting indices in an infinite word is not a requirement that the entire occurrence lie inside the finite prefix, and the transform-avoidance results are not statements about this frequency.

evidence: Start/length data can be translated to endings by adding the full occurrence length minus one. Even reversal of a dyadic prefix only pairs contained occurrences: starts whose squares cross the prefix boundary must be removed. The proof instead counts endpoints by desubstitution, subtracts the two length-four exceptions in the reduced word and keeps boundary terms in the halving counts.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The exact square classification is acknowledged prior input. Turning it into the explicit all-depth arithmetic law requires the endpoint and boundary analysis; the known automaton or existence of a finite algorithm is not itself an exact count theorem for that statistic.

originality.rationale: The supported claim is the exact parity-sensitive dyadic count and quantitative arbitrary-prefix law for direct-prefix curling numbers. The frequency 1/6 is not credited as a new prediction; it was explicitly suggested in OEIS. The closest structural result classifies and counts squares by starting index in the infinite word, not suffixes constrained to lie in each prefix. The searched Resultary match is the bound result itself. The comparisons are bounded and do not establish absolute priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent derivation or a further exact analysis of the known automata may exist. The arbitrary-prefix bound is not claimed to be sharp.

value.rationale: The classic curling transform already motivated a concrete frequency question. Counting the square-free suffix endpoints resolves it and quantifies the discrepancy. Powers of two are the intrinsic scales of the substitution rather than an arbitrary subsequence, and the parity-dependent correction describes a precise finite-scale obstruction to exact density on those scales.
